tasks.short: File finance records, handle calls, and prepare routine correspondence.

steps.what: Receive and sort incoming finance correspondence and documents.

loop.input: Incoming correspondence, attachment metadata, and approved routing categories.
loop.output: Proposed category, record reference, and destination.
loop.check: Require an allowed category and valid destination; validate record references against authorised records.
loop.stop: One classification attempt per item; ambiguous references or categories enter the clerk's exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sender rules handle known streams; varied free-text requests still need interpretation.

steps.what: Index documents and file them against the relevant finance record.
Answer calls, establish the request, and provide information or transfer the caller.
Prepare routine acknowledgements and correspondence using approved wording and finance records.
Check the recipient and content, then send and retain the correspondence.

tasks.design: Configure filing between {EMAIL}, {DOCS}, and {ERP}, with a bounded classifier for unfamiliar correspondence and an exception queue in {WORKFLOW}. Generate routine drafts from approved templates and verified records, then require recipient and content approval before sending through {EMAIL}. Keep calls human, supported by a contact directory and linked account answers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Filing references and routing knowledge lived in individual inboxes. Templates lacked reliable links to finance records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing filing rules cover known streams. AI-assisted coding makes the connectors and template generator cheaper to build; bounded classification covers remaining free text.
tasks.still_hard: Poor references, confidential attachments, and callers with several intertwined concerns still require attention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising urgency, calming a frustrated caller, and noticing when routine wording would mislead.

ambition.what: A finance request receipt showing the responsible team and expected response date.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from sorting and filing toward resolving misrouted requests and handling calls. The clerk can assign routine requests within an agreed routing matrix; authority over financial commitments does not change.

reach.task: Link customer correspondence to billing records.
reach.learn: Billing references, recipient permissions, and the difference between an acknowledgement and a payment commitment.

reach.task: Apply retention schedules to finance correspondence.
reach.learn: Retention categories, access restrictions, and exceptions requiring preservation.

evidence.claim: Rule-based filing and template generation are feasible; this design and its time estimates are proposals.
The cited survey found paper or email invoice approvals common, supporting an inbox-handoff assumption.

assumptions: These are typical steps and estimated time shares, not measured customer activity.
Physical post is occasional; regular paper intake would add scanning work.
The prior understates correspondence work for this finance-specific task; calls remain a substantial human share.
GDPR applies to personal data. EU AI Act duties depend on the deployed use; national rules determine employee consultation requirements.
Build ranges describe an initial departmental rollout with usable interfaces, including access review and consultation where required.
unknowns: Document retention rules and available record identifiers.
The actual split between calls, electronic correspondence, and paper.
Whether mailbox and document-store access is already approved.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed routing or logging.
research_questions: Can existing filing configuration attach documents to finance records without custom code?
Which incoming categories cannot be routed reliably using sender and reference rules?
new_work: Review ambiguous routing and missing record references.
Maintain correspondence templates and the contact directory.
Check filing failures, retention settings, and access permissions.

tasks.short: Find financial records and answer general or account-specific questions.

steps.what: Clarify the question, identify the account, and verify the requester's entitlement.
Retrieve account balances, transactions, and payment status.
Check supporting documents and reconcile apparent differences in the account record.
Write an answer explaining the verified figures and any unresolved issue.

loop.input: Verified query and permission-filtered facts with source references.
loop.output: Answer draft with each financial assertion linked to a source.
loop.check: Validate all amounts, dates, account references, and source links; prohibit unsupported explanations.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unresolved discrepancies receive a factual holding response for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover common questions; varied questions need short explanations assembled from several facts.

steps.what: Approve and send the response, or refer the unresolved issue to an accountant.

tasks.design: Expose approved account views from {ERP}, with supporting links from {DOCS} and permission checks at retrieval. Deterministic checks assemble verified facts; templates answer standard queries and a bounded loop drafts varied explanations. A {WORKFLOW} queue handles discrepancies, while a clerk approves outgoing responses through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account views, attachments, and permissions were fragmented. Generic search could retrieve figures without establishing whether they answered the question.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured account views and inexpensive connectors reduce retrieval work. Bounded drafting can explain a verified fact bundle without performing financial calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Unposted transactions, disputed balances, and unclear requester authority remain difficult. A technically correct balance can still need accounting interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding what the requester needs and explaining uncertainty without implying an unsupported financial commitment.

ambition.what: Permission-scoped invoice-status self-service for budget holders.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving discrepancies and less time searching screens. They can deliver approved factual answers faster; authority to amend accounts or settle disputes does not change.

reach.task: Assemble an account history for a credit review.
reach.learn: Ageing definitions, disputed items, and the limits of factual reporting versus credit decisions.
Record access, refresh timing, and definitions of posted, paid, and outstanding.

evidence.claim: Permission-filtered financial retrieval and source-checked answer drafting are feasible; the combined service is a proposed design.
AFAS documents matching bank lines to records using references, IBAN, or invoice numbers, with misses handled by people.

assumptions: These are typical steps and estimated time shares, not measured customer activity.
Most requested figures already exist as structured records in the {ERP}.
The prior's near-total automation estimate is optimistic when questions include unclear identity, disputes, or interpretation.
The self-service ambition starts with authorised internal budget holders and approved factual views.
GDPR applies to account-related personal data. EU AI Act classification depends on use; this service does not decide natural-person creditworthiness.
Build ranges include access review and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Available account views, interfaces, and document links.
Which requesters may see which account details.
The share of questions requiring accounting interpretation.
Whether budget holders already have suitable self-service access.
research_questions: Which questions can an existing {ERP} account view answer directly?
Can every answer fact carry a stable record reference and freshness timestamp?
new_work: Review explanatory drafts and approve outgoing responses.
Resolve stale data, missing documents, and disputed balances.
Maintain approved query types and answer templates.
Test permissions when roles or account ownership change.

tasks.short: Classify transactions, prepare journals, and maintain financial records and summaries.

steps.what: Gather source transactions and supporting documents for recording.
Check completeness and assign routine ledger, tax, and cost-centre codes.
Resolve ambiguous accounting treatment and authorise exceptional coding.
Prepare balanced journal entries from routine and authorised exceptional coding.
Review and approve manual journals and material exceptions.
Post validated entries and produce ledger summaries.

tasks.design: Connect source records and attachments to {ERP}, then configure completeness checks, coding defaults, balanced journals, and ledger summaries. Route ambiguous treatment and manual journal approval through {WORKFLOW}; post routine entries under approved rules and exceptional entries only after their required approval. Retain source references and posting logs for correction and audit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source feeds were inconsistent, coding rules were partly tacit, and exceptional entries travelled outside the posting workflow.
tasks.enabler_now: Most accounting checks already exist in the {ERP}. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of source adapters and exception handling without changing accounting policy.
tasks.still_hard: New transaction types, tax treatment, cut-off, and capitalisation require accounting judgement. Duplicate prevention and recovery after partial imports need careful testing.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising economic substance and identifying when a familiar-looking transaction needs different accounting treatment.

ambition.what: A daily accountant decision on unresolved cut-off and coding exceptions.

tasks.altitude: The clerk works an exception queue and checks source completeness instead of repeatedly entering journals. They can clear evidenced clerical errors within delegated limits; accountants retain policy and material judgement decisions.

reach.task: Prepare evidence for cut-off and classification decisions.
reach.learn: Accruals, capitalisation, materiality, and when a correction needs approval.

reach.task: Identify recurring causes of late or misclassified transactions.
reach.learn: Close dependencies, control ownership, and how to distinguish source defects from accounting policy issues.

evidence.claim: Configured coding, balanced journal generation, and ledger summaries are established accounting capabilities; implementation estimates are proposals.
Medius supports line-level invoice, order, and receipt matching, providing an upstream source-validation example.
The Huuskes vendor case reports automatically processed invoices increasing from 40% to 65%; it does not establish general-ledger automation rates.

assumptions: These are typical steps and estimated time shares, not measured customer activity.
Most inputs are structured; upstream invoice extraction is not rebuilt within this task.
Routine entries can post under approved rules; manual journals and material exceptions require the stated approvals.
Human treatment and approval steps include adjacent-role time in the end-to-end task.
This task overlaps ledger calculation and correction work in task 43-3031.00:2489; their savings must not be added without removing overlap.
GDPR applies where records contain personal data. EU AI Act duties depend on use, and employee consultation follows national rules.
Build ranges include accounting configuration, access approval, and consultation where required.
unknowns: Transaction sources, volumes, and existing coding coverage.
Delegated correction limits and journal approval policy.
Available import controls, reversal functions, and audit logs.
The actual split of clerk and accountant effort.
research_questions: Which source transactions can use existing {ERP} posting profiles?
Can imports prevent duplicates and recover safely after interrupted posting?
Which exception categories require judgement rather than another deterministic rule?
new_work: Investigate missing sources, rejected imports, and duplicate warnings.
Maintain coding mappings when accounts or cost centres change.
Review exceptional coding and manual journals.
Reconcile imported transaction counts and values to posting logs.

tasks.short: Calculate debit and credit totals, reconcile balances, and process approved corrections.

steps.what: Select the accounts, entity, and period for the balance check.
Export ledger balances into a reconciliation workbook.
Calculate debit totals, credit totals, and opening-to-closing balances.
Compare totals with control balances and identify discrepancies.
Investigate discrepancies and prepare supported correcting entries.
Review the proposed correction and approve its accounting treatment.
Post approved corrections and refresh the balance check.

tasks.design: Use configured {ERP} reports to calculate debit, credit, and closing balances directly, removing the duplicate {SPREADSHEET} export. Add deterministic control comparisons on {DATA_PLATFORM}, with an exception view in {BI} linked to supporting records in {DOCS}. Accountants approve correcting entries in {ERP}; posting then refreshes the checks automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workbook checks bridged gaps between standard reports and local control definitions. Exporting became routine even where the underlying arithmetic was already available.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reports handle the arithmetic. AI-assisted coding makes the small control adapter and exception view cheaper to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Balanced debits and credits do not prove correct classification, completeness, or cut-off. Explaining a discrepancy often requires source investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a harmless timing difference from an error that changes the financial picture.

ambition.what: Daily triage of newly unreconciled control accounts.

tasks.altitude: The clerk reviews new balance exceptions instead of rebuilding workbooks. They can prioritise investigations using agreed materiality and age limits; approval rights over correcting journals do not change.

reach.task: Prepare control-account reconciliation evidence for the close.
reach.learn: Reconciliation assertions, timing differences, cut-off, and correction versus reversal.

reach.task: Prioritise unresolved balance exceptions before reporting.
reach.learn: Materiality, exception ageing, and dependencies that could delay the close.

evidence.claim: Ledger totals and trial-balance arithmetic are standard accounting configuration; bespoke control comparisons can use deterministic code.
AFAS documents deterministic matching with human handling of misses; this supports the exception-handling pattern, not all ledger reconciliation claims.

assumptions: These are typical steps and estimated time shares, not measured customer activity.
The {ERP} performs ordinary double-entry arithmetic; the workbook supports selected reconciliation checks rather than the whole ledger.
The task wording supports more spreadsheet work than its prior, but existing system calculations should be reused.
Investigation remains human even though evidence retrieval and draft-entry preparation become faster.
Shared journals, approvals, and posting work overlap task 43-3031.00:2490 and must not be counted twice.
GDPR applies to personal data in drill-down records. EU AI Act duties depend on deployed use; employee consultation follows national rules.
Build ranges include access review and consultation where required.
unknowns: Which workbook checks are already available in the {ERP}.
Definitions and authoritative sources of control balances.
Whether reporting includes multiple entities or currencies.
Correction approval thresholds and period-lock rules.
research_questions: Can configured {ERP} reports replace the reconciliation export completely?
Which discrepancies can deterministic checks explain without proposing an accounting correction?
Can refreshes use a consistent ledger snapshot to avoid false differences?
new_work: Review newly flagged differences and record their explanations.
Maintain control definitions and reporting scope.
Approve corrections and resolve locked-period exceptions.
Check that control data and ledger snapshots remain aligned.

role.altitude: The week shifts from retrieval, copying, and arithmetic toward source-quality checks, exception investigation, and clear financial explanations. Delegated clerical correction and routing rights can expand within explicit limits; accounting policy, material journal approval, and financial commitments remain with authorised roles.
reach: Accountant: prepare supported reconciliations and classification proposals.
Financial manager: explain recurring exceptions and their effect on reporting readiness.
Business intelligence analyst: define traceable, permission-scoped financial views.
skills_to_grow: Configuration, rule maintenance, and bounded-model output review.
role.ambitious_version: A finance operations specialist who provides daily visibility into unresolved posting and balance issues, prepares evidence for accountant decisions, and delivers permission-scoped account answers.
